claims.statement: The supplied text introduces Anita Morjani/Moorjani and a podcast host addressed as Julie; recording identity, date and alignment remain unverified.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: Reliable access to supplied text; provenance is not authentication.

claims.statement: Moorjani describes lymphoma, rapid tumor reduction and discharge after five weeks; her assertion that she has records is not inspection of pathology, treatments or objective recovery measurements.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: Treatment chronology and cause of recovery unknown from inspected material. No spontaneous-remission or no-chemotherapy conclusion.

claims.statement: Moorjani recounts recognizing a doctor and hearing a hallway prognosis, and describes a later critical newspaper interview plus supportive doctors; these are her retellings of other people’s statements.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: Neither named critic nor supportive clinician was independently interviewed here. Quoted surprise is not independent corroboration.

claims.statement: Smit2008 traces the dentures narrative through a1991 Meijers article and a February1994 Addink interview with nurse TG, then his own2008 follow-up.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: The earliest identified1991 text and full1994 Dutch notes were not directly inspected.

claims.statement: Smit reports K.B. identified himself as a messenger between TG and Meijers, rather than a participant in the resuscitation; repeated interviews remain dependent on TG.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: Supported as source attribution only; external event verification remains limited.

claims.statement: Woerlee dates the dentures event to late1979 and recounts unresponsiveness, ventricular fibrillation, CPR and later recovery from the published nurse narrative; these are not newly inspected clinical measurements.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: Exact event date, collapse-to-CPR duration, core temperature and raw monitoring records unavailable.

claims.statement: In Smit’s translated nurse account, the patient later identifies TG and a distinctive cart/shelf associated with the dentures; investigators did not obtain a direct patient interview.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: Reported recognition is specific testimony; its first wording and prior information access are not independently established.

claims.statement: Smit identifies a stop-CPR versus continue-CPR discrepancy and reports TG’s later explanation as two successive phases: pain first, then fear of premature cessation.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: Later reconciliation is not an independently timestamped resolution.

claims.statement: Smit and Rivas acknowledge dependence on one principal witness and state that official medical records had been destroyed; the present audit has no measured EEG interval for the dentures perception.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: Destruction is the authors’ statement, not an independent records-retention audit. References to absent cortex activity are inference, not a supplied tracing.

claims.statement: Woerlee proposes preserved or restored sensory awareness during hypothermia/CPR, recognizable voice, sensation and later reconstruction as an ordinary account of the dentures report.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: Proposed physiology and detailed prehospital sequence were not measured in this case; the cited general clinical studies were not newly audited.

claims.statement: Smit and Rivas reply that TG placed dentures removal before restarting the Thumper, and that a pre-opened wooden shelf undermines an explanation relying on hearing a metal drawer.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: Reply depends on TG’s later sequence and spatial description; it does not independently exclude every sensory or later-learning route.

claims.statement: The defender texts differ on pain: Smit2008 allows restored circulation/physical pain; Smit–Rivas2010 first proposes psychogenic extrasensory pain but also allows mixed physical and extrasensory input if TG’s cortical assessment was mistaken.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: A change in interpretation and assumptions, not two independently established physiological observations.

claims.statement: The Reynolds sources place aneurysm surgery in August1991 and give a sequence of anesthesia, skull opening, bypass/cooling, circulatory arrest, rewarming and closure. Carter supplies clock times through Sabom’s account.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: Clock times and drugs are attributed chronology; original operative/anesthesia/EEG/BAEP records not inspected.

claims.statement: Carter reproduces Reynolds’s descriptions of a toothbrush-like surgical tool, its case, a vessel-size exchange and an apparent encounter with relatives; the narrative and subsequent matching depend substantially on Sabom’s account.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: Raw initial description, complete errors/misses and before-feedback record not inspected. A visual description is not independently verified out-of-body vision.

claims.statement: Carter explicitly places the externally checkable early perceptions before absent brainstem response; Hameroff conditionally agrees the four auditory examples occurred under anesthesia rather than hypothermic circulatory arrest.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: Agreement about published phase assignment is not additional physiological measurement or a timestamp for the relatives/light experience.

claims.statement: Woerlee reports Sabom first contacted Reynolds in1994; Carter says she first mentioned the experience to Spetzler several days after surgery. Neither inspected2011 paper supplies a contemporaneous verbatim first account.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: Early disclosure, later investigation and1998 publication must remain different dates. Sabom1998 chapter and2002 documentary not directly inspected.

claims.statement: Woerlee argues ordinary hearing remained possible despite clicks/earpieces and infers awareness plus drug-shaped experience, partly importing parameters from related published surgical protocols.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: Generic procedure parameters are not this patient’s measured drug concentrations or auditory thresholds. Possibility and actual cause are distinct.

claims.statement: Hameroff grants a possible awareness explanation conditional on the portrayal being accurate, but questions the absent raw BAER results and reliance on monitoring error; he does not claim particular-case expertise.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: His characterization of BAER as definitive is an attributed position, not adopted contemporary clinical guidance; credentials do not settle the tracing.

claims.statement: Carter argues that vivid visual details, the missing reported clicks, sealing/masking and brainstem-versus-conscious perception distinctions challenge Woerlee’s account, and proposes a calibrated reconstruction.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: No completed reconstruction result inspected. Phenomenological difference alone does not exclude ordinary generation. Reputation/ideology rhetoric is not case evidence.

claims.statement: Carter quotes Cordova on technical parameters and explicitly locates Cordova in the adjacent operating room; Cordova’s quoted statement calls for an experiment and does not itself establish whether Reynolds heard.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: Near-primary technical correspondence via Carter; original messages and the monitoring colleague’s record are not independently inspected.

claims.statement: The two dossiers support specific, traceable perception claims and substantive disputes, but lack independently fixed perception timing plus complete information-access controls needed to identify extracerebral acquisition.
alternative_explanations: Ordinary perception during residual/restored processing
Retrospective reconstruction or later information
Anomalous perception under additional verified timing and independence assumptions
limitations: Project assessment, not a claim that an ordinary explanation has been demonstrated.

claims.statement: Resuscitation reports do not by themselves establish the same person’s subjectivity beyond irreversible death, fundamental mind, universal subjecthood or timelessness.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: Project application of T01 definitions and T13 identity distinctions.

claims.statement: Recovery after CPR or surgery, and an interview’s temporal association of insight with improvement, do not alone establish miraculous or consciousness-caused healing.
alternative_explanations: Attribution of a report or argument does not establish its described event or conclusion.
limitations: No treatment efficacy, disease prognosis, spontaneous-remission rate or medical advice is inferred.

arguments.name: Dentures conditional anomalous-perception argument
premises: In Smit’s translated nurse account, the patient later identifies TG and a distinctive cart/shelf associated with the dentures; investigators did not obtain a direct patient interview.
Smit and Rivas acknowledge dependence on one principal witness and state that official medical records had been destroyed; the present audit has no measured EEG interval for the dentures perception.
Smit and Rivas reply that TG placed dentures removal before restarting the Thumper, and that a pre-opened wooden shelf undermines an explanation relying on hearing a metal drawer.
bridge_principles: A verified acquisition episode incompatible with a specified dependence model challenges that model only when timing, identity and information-access premises hold.
arguments.conclusion: If the report and exclusion/timing premises hold, the specific neural-dependence model would be challenged.
arguments.strongest_objection: Single-witness retrospective timing and information control are insufficient to establish those premises.
arguments.strongest_reply: Unusual shelf details and pre-Thumper removal deserve testing; a generic ordinary possibility does not erase the report.
unresolved_issues: No defensible numerical likelihood ratio or posterior; dependence on shared case narratives retained.

arguments.name: Reynolds conditional anomalous-perception argument
premises: Carter reproduces Reynolds’s descriptions of a toothbrush-like surgical tool, its case, a vessel-size exchange and an apparent encounter with relatives; the narrative and subsequent matching depend substantially on Sabom’s account.

Carter explicitly places the externally checkable early perceptions before absent brainstem response; Hameroff conditionally agrees the four auditory examples occurred under anesthesia rather than hypothermic circulatory arrest.

Carter argues that vivid visual details, the missing reported clicks, sealing/masking and brainstem-versus-conscious perception distinctions challenge Woerlee’s account, and proposes a calibrated reconstruction.

Carter quotes Cordova on technical parameters and explicitly locates Cordova in the adjacent operating room; Cordova’s quoted statement calls for an experiment and does not itself establish whether Reynolds heard.
bridge_principles: A verified acquisition episode incompatible with a specified dependence model challenges that model only when timing, identity and information-access premises hold.
arguments.conclusion: If precise perception and independently established exclusion conditions coincide, the case favors acquisition beyond the specified normal channels.
arguments.strongest_objection: Checkable claims occur outside the alleged standstill interval, and drug/monitoring/access conditions are incompletely inspected.
arguments.strongest_reply: Carter’s technical details and visual specificity challenge simplistic hearing reconstructions; neither party has supplied the decisive controlled comparison here.
unresolved_issues: No defensible numerical likelihood ratio or posterior; dependence on shared case narratives retained.

arguments.name: Limit of survival and cosmic extrapolation
premises: The two dossiers support specific, traceable perception claims and substantive disputes, but lack independently fixed perception timing plus complete information-access controls needed to identify extracerebral acquisition.
Resuscitation reports do not by themselves establish the same person’s subjectivity beyond irreversible death, fundamental mind, universal subjecthood or timelessness.
bridge_principles: Temporary independence does not automatically establish irreversible-death survival or cosmic/normative attributes.
arguments.conclusion: Neither dossier establishes the full enduring/timeless conscious-foundation package.
arguments.strongest_objection: A verified brain-independent episode could nevertheless be relevant to models permitting personal survival.
arguments.strongest_reply: Relevance is retained conditionally; irreversible death, numerical identity, universal subjecthood, purpose and normative relations require additional premises.
unresolved_issues: No defensible numerical likelihood ratio or posterior; dependence on shared case narratives retained.
